title: Tsallis-entropy analogue of the AM-GM information identity
problemStatement: Establish the Tsallis-entropy analogue of the entropy identity underlying the AM-GM / Rényi lineage (parent amgm-inequality-oq-03-oq-04, H_α = −log(M_{α−1})), replacing the geometric/log operations by the q-deformed arithmetic ones, and identify the equality/limit cases recovering the Shannon case as q → 1.
currentState: COMPLETED. A self-contained, fully machine-checked Lean file (0 sorries, 0 axioms) formalizes the q-logarithm ln_q, Tsallis entropy S_q, and five results: (i) the pseudo-additive law of ln_q, (ii) the escort identity S_q = −Σ pᵢ^q·ln_q(pᵢ), (iii) the Rényi bridge S_q = ln_q(exp(H_q)), (iv) non-extensivity S_q(p⊗r) = S_q(p)+S_q(r)+(1−q)·S_q(p)·S_q(r), and (v) the q→1 limit ln_q(x) → log(x) recovering Shannon.
knownResults: Tsallis (1988): non-extensive entropy S_q generalizing Boltzmann-Gibbs/Shannon.
Rényi (1961): H_α family, with H_1 = Shannon as α→1.
references: Tsallis, C. (1988). Possible generalization of Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics. J. Stat. Phys. 52, 479-487.
Rényi, A. (1961). On measures of entropy and information. 4th Berkeley Symp.

insights: The parent's exp/log pair generalizes to the q-exponential/q-logarithm pair: H_α = −log(M_{α−1}) becomes S_q = ln_q(exp(H_q)). The two entropies are the same information content under this deformation.

The q-logarithm obeys a pseudo-additive product law ln_q(xy) = ln_q(x)+ln_q(y)+(1−q)·ln_q(x)·ln_q(y); the single cross term (1−q)·ln_q(x)·ln_q(y) is the entire content of non-extensivity and vanishes as q→1.
Tsallis entropy is Shannon's −Σ pᵢ log pᵢ under TWO simultaneous replacements: log→ln_q AND probabilities re-weighted by escort powers pᵢ^q. Both are required for the escort identity to close.
Non-extensivity S_q(p⊗r) = S_q(p)+S_q(r)+(1−q)·S_q(p)·S_q(r) is an EXACT algebraic identity, reducing entirely to the factorization Σ (pᵢrⱼ)^q = (Σpᵢ^q)(Σrⱼ^q) of the escort sum.
The q→1 Shannon recovery is literally a derivative: ln_q(x) is the finite-difference slope at 0 of u↦x^u, whose limiting slope is log x. Proved via hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope on 𝓝[≠] 1.
